problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=2x-3{y}^{2}+z$ that passes through the point $P(1,1,1).$
worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,1,1) & =2(1)-3({1}^{2})+1 \\  & =2-3+1 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ 2x-3{y}^{2}+z & =0 \\ z & =3{y}^{2}-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(1,1,1)$ is the surface $z=3{y}^{2}-2x.$
